editorial:
Prom Night (2008) takes the classic slasher setup and gives it a glossy, modern makeover. You follow Donna, a high school senior who is finally ready to move on from a terrible tragedy in her past. Her big night at prom turns into a nightmare when a killer from her history shows up to ruin everything. The movie leans hard into teen drama and suspense, with plenty of pretty dresses, loud music, and dark hallways. It is not the scariest horror film out there, but it keeps you guessing about who might be next and what will happen to her friends.

The cast, led by Brittany Snow, does a solid job of selling the fear and panic throughout the night. The pacing moves quickly, jumping from one tense moment to the next without much downtime. Some scenes feel a bit predictable, but the energy never really drops. If you enjoy slasher movies with a focus on characters and a fast-moving plot, this one is easy to get into. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: The killer turns out to be Richard Fenton, Donna's former teacher who murdered her family years ago and has now escaped. He stalks Donna and her friends through the hotel, killing several of them. In the final scenes, Richard breaks into Donna's home and attacks her and her aunt. Police arrive just in time and shoot Richard dead. Donna survives the night, but the trauma of her past and prom night stays with her.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves slasher movies and teen thrillers.
